First, to simplify the fraction on the left-hand side, we multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6-7\text{i}}{3-2\text{i}} & =2p-5q\text{i} \\ \frac{(6-7\text{i})(3+2\text{i})}{(3-2\text{i})(3+2\text{i})} & =2p-5q\text{i} \\ \frac{18+12\text{i}-21\text{i}-14{\text{i}}^{2}}{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}} & =2p-5q\text{i} \\ \frac{18-9\text{i}-14(-1)}{13} & =2p-5q\text{i} \\ \frac{32-9\text{i}}{13} & =2p-5q\text{i} \\ \frac{32}{13}-\frac{9}{13}\text{i} & =2p-5q\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can equate the real parts and the imaginary parts separately.

- Equating the real parts, we get $\frac{32}{13}=2p.$

- Equating the imaginary parts, we get $-\frac{9}{13}=-5q.$

Therefore, $p=\frac{16}{13}$ and $q=\frac{9}{65}.$
